claim: Vercel now reports that coding agents initiate more than half of deployments on its platform, indicating that agent-driven software delivery has crossed from edge case to routine infrastructure load.
verifiedFacts: Vercel's Agentic Infrastructure page currently states that, as of September 2026, more than 50% of deployments are initiated by coding agents, up from more than 30% earlier in 2026.
inference: Repository governance, preview isolation, CI evidence, scoped write permissions, and rollback receipts need to be designed for machine-generated change as a default condition.
Consultancy: agentic delivery-control review can be packaged around branch policy, preview environments, tests, provenance, rollback, and human promotion gates.

Disposition: Seed Loom CORE; Project Constellation PRODUCTIZE for portfolio evidence; AETHER and design-system repos should adopt shared machine-change receipts rather than independent governance stacks.
significance: The operating environment for web engineering is changing: machine-generated code is no longer exceptional, so control surfaces must move closer to the repository and deployment boundary.
assumptions: Vercel's customer mix is directionally informative for modern web-development workflows.
knownLimitations: The metric is provider-reported, platform-specific, and does not by itself measure code quality, review burden, or business value.
